clue.text: Song about little back room to spare

indicators.note: the song's letters go round the other piece, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: back tells us to read the small word from right to left

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for little

explanation.surface: A lyric about a tiny back room kept free for guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns WEE into EEW, and 'about' puts LAY round it: L-EEW-AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is slack or margin, extra space allowed beyond what is strictly needed.

clue.text: Float, though screwed at vital tee

indicators.note: screwed means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golf ball floats away even though it was firmly screwed down on its tee.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is VITAL TEE, eight letters; 'though' and 'at' only link the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise and hover in the air, which is to float.

clue.text: I mix with secret love — very secret!

indicators.note: mix asks for the letters gathered here to be stirred into a new order

parts.note: love means nil in tennis scores, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone mingles with a hidden lover, an affair kept extremely quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: I, SECRET and O (love) are shuffled together to give the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, hence highly private.

clue.text: Get off with a blonde

parts.note: blonde hair is light in colour

explanation.surface: A suggestive line about getting off with a fair-haired person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off' reads as a chat-up idiom, but it is the definition: to step down from a bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to step down from a vehicle, synonym for dismount.

clue.text: Beast of burden might muck about inside the enclosure

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the walls of the other

parts.note: a pale is an area enclosed by a fence of stakes

indicators.note: about here means in a jumble, so these four letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An animal kept in a pen might mess around in there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles MUCK to CKMU, and 'inside' puts that within PALE: PA-CKMU-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack mule is a hybrid animal used to carry loads, the classic beast of burden.

clue.text: Sharp to provide help when caught inside

indicators.note: inside signals that one letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: aid means help
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Sharp-witted help is given when someone is trapped indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective means sour or tart, sharp in taste or tone.

clue.text: The WI talk to doctors on a powerful measure

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute lecture to medics on some potent remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation; here its letters are simply part of the fodder WI TALK TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a unit of power, a thousand watts, so it measures power.

clue.text: A French fellow on ecstasy was seduced

parts.note: un is the French for a
a don is a fellow of a university college
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Frenchman high on drugs was lured into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Undone in an old-fashioned sense means ruined, a woman brought down by a seducer.

clue.text: Team appearing one by one

explanation.surface: A team turning up one player at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 11 is written as a 1 standing beside a 1, so 'one by one' describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides have that many players, and the numeral is two ones side by side.

clue.text: Instrument for mixing oil with Chardonnay, perhaps

indicators.note: with here means held within, so the shuffled letters go inside the wine

parts.note: Chardonnay is an example of wine, vin in French

indicators.note: mixing asks for the three letters to be stirred into another order

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool for stirring oil into white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' turns OIL into IOL, which goes inside VIN: V-IOL-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin is a stringed instrument played with a bow.

clue.text: One's left in American car to drive out

indicators.note: in places the short pieces inside the car's name

parts.note: Dodge is an American car make
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: Someone stays behind in a US car, ready to drive off.
explanation.walkthrough: IS and L go together inside DODGE: D-ISL-ODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of its place, to expel or evict it.

clue.text: Is Guinness non-U? Give it a shake when one flags

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the contents, so the remaining letters are rearranged
non- before a letter tells us to do without it

parts.note: U is the letter named

explanation.surface: Is a stout not posh? Shake it up when you are tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is a British term for not upper class; here it means remove U from GUINNESS, leaving GINNESS, which 'Give it a shake' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensigns are banners, particularly those flown by ships to show nationality.

clue.text: Support the object of developing a bite

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Holding up the purpose of growing a set of jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby cutting its first set of chompers is growing the means to chew.

clue.text: Painful effect of putting lots of aircraft into initial training exercises

indicators.note: into means one piece is put within the other
initial picks the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: a wing is an air force unit made up of many aircraft

explanation.surface: The ache that comes from adding squadrons to the opening drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes T and E from TRAINING EXERCISES, and WING goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pang of pain.

clue.text: Fine levied primarily on debtors — such bloomers

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so take only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: debtors are people who owe, owers

explanation.surface: A penalty charged mainly to those in debt for such howlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests blunders or underwear, but here it is things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants in bloom produce blossoms, so a bloomer is something that blossoms.

clue.text: Catch on a little branch

explanation.surface: Snagging on a small branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for to understand, and a twig is a small shoot of a tree.

clue.text: Accounts of alien getting in soldiers' lodgings

indicators.note: getting in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: bills are accounts of money owed
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: Records of a foreigner getting into army quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Billets are quarters assigned to troops in private houses.

clue.text: He mixes with prince to use the code

indicators.note: mixes asks for the two words' letters to be blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A man mingles with royalty to follow the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To encipher is to convert a message into secret writing.

clue.text: Took away a book, the old penny cut-out edition

parts.note: D was the symbol for the old British penny, from Latin denarius

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone takes away a book, a cut-out edition worth an old penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-out' looks like one word; 'out' is the anagram signal turning CUT into UCT.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, so abducted means seized and removed.

clue.text: Had a topping time

parts.note: topping reads as great fun but also means cutting off the top, here a person's head

explanation.definitionFit: Someone executed by the axe had their head cut off, a literal topping.

clue.text: Not widely recognised and sunk without son's present name

indicators.note: without tells us to remove a letter from the word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
now is the present time

explanation.surface: An obscure figure, drowned without his boy, now has a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking S out of SUNK leaves UNK; then add NOW and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure or unfamiliar is not known to most people.

clue.text: Can find drink around the beachhead

indicators.note: around means the drink is wrapped round the other letter

parts.note: ale is a drink
the head, or first letter, of beach is B

explanation.surface: You can find a drink near where the troops landed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able is to have the power to, as in can do.

clue.text: Way the fliers start to encounter fire from machine guns

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's fliers

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Airmen meet machine-gun fire along the route.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Past his best, first defender managed to get rid of the ball

definitions.text: managed to get rid of the ball

parts.note: passe means out of date, past its prime

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An ageing defender still managed to pass the ball on.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a player who has moved the ball on to a teammate has given it away.

clue.text: What's in it is secret, but it gives one the picture

explanation.surface: Something whose contents are confidential yet which shows you everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in camera' means in private, as a court hearing held behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera means in private, and a photographic device produces images.

clue.text: Sad time to bring back subject of smoking

indicators.note: bring back tells us to turn the following word round

parts.note: a cigar is something smoked

explanation.surface: A sorry occasion when smoking is raised again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring back' turns CIGAR into RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means dreadfully unhappy or sorrowful.

clue.text: Tear jerker with undoubted riches

indicators.note: a jerker pulls things about, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain, undoubted

explanation.surface: A weepie film that surely brings a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear jerker' reads as a sad film; 'jerker' rearranges TEAR to TREA, followed by SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a store of wealth, such as gold or jewels.

clue.text: Second time the Yorkshire borders have been an eyesore

indicators.note: borders means the outside letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Once more the edges of Yorkshire have been ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes the first and last letters of YORKSHIRE, Y and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, quite literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Others tease the lover of beauty

indicators.note: others means other forms, so the letters of the following words are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Some people mock the person who adores beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Others' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal for TEASE THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person with a cultivated appreciation of art and beauty.

clue.text: Gave a blow to a sort of lord

explanation.surface: Striking a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: A belted earl is a British title: an earl invested with a sword belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Belted is slang for hit hard, and a belted earl is a nobleman of a particular kind.

clue.text: Backed last horse: it lost its head and died

parts.note: end means last part

indicators.note: lost its head means the first letter of the horse is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone backed the final horse, but it fell and died.
explanation.walkthrough: HORSE without its first letter is ORSE, between END and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or approve, as one does a candidate.

clue.text: Open prison worked

parts.note: can is slang for prison
did means carried out, worked

explanation.surface: An open prison has functioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and outspoken, honest and direct.
